deadline.value: International Round 1 (31 August) for starts by 31 March 2027 has closed; the College's Round 2 closes 15 April 2027 (year inferred) for starts by 31 August 2027. Submit at least two weeks early so referees can respond.
deadline.quote: Round 1 International | The closing date for the international main round is 31 August each year, for research students commencing in the following year by 31 March. | Round 2 (international and domestic) | The College holds an additional research scholarship round that closes 15 April each year, for research students commencing in the same year by 31 August.

also.quote: We recommend submitting your application at least two weeks prior to scholarship application deadlines to give your referees time to provide their references for you.

supervisor.value: A supervisor in the ANU School of Engineering must be available and willing to supervise you, and you need an identified research project before applying.
supervisor.quote: There must be a supervisor at the ANU College of Engineering and Computer Science who is available and willing to supervise your research, and you must have identified a research project.

also.quote: Regardless of the quality of the application, you cannot be accepted into an ANU Engineering research program without having the support of an ANU Engineering researcher willing to supervise you.

funding.value: Stipend scholarships are allocated competitively through the central rounds (you are considered automatically). The RTP stipend is AUD 40,475 a year (2027 base rate). International tuition is AUD 58,925.00 a year (indicative).
funding.quote: HDR living stipend scholarships are allocated following a competitive process.

also.quote: $ 40,475 per annum (Full-time base RTP stipend rate 2027)
Annual indicative fee for international students | $58,925.00

entry_route.value: A relevant four-year undergraduate degree (honours level, H2A or above; first-class often required) or a postgraduate degree with a significant research thesis.
entry_route.quote: To be eligible for admission to the Doctor of Philosophy program you should have completed a relevant four-year undergraduate degree from an eligible university, or a postgraduate qualification with a significant research thesis component. | An Australian Bachelor degree with at least Second Class Honours - Upper (First Class Honours is often required) or its international equivalent, or

notes: One Engineering PhD (academic plan 9715XPHD) across the school's research areas: Aerospace, Energy, Environmental, Information & Signal Processing, Mechatronics.
